authorization: owner ruling: add one narrow Allow sts:AssumeRole for exactly the governed reader role; do not change the reader trust policy
why: the reader trust policy delegates to the ACCOUNT ROOT with a condition on aws:PrincipalArn; when a trust policy delegates to root, the caller's identity policy must also grant sts:AssumeRole. Removing the Deny alone left the decision at implicitDeny.

binding_precondition_check.whose: the READER role mr002-validation-reader, inline policy mr002-validation-only
binding_precondition_check.verdict: no stop condition — the host inline policy is not hash-bound by any governing artifact
binding_precondition_check.caveat: the canonicalisation used for those reader hashes could not be reproduced locally, so NO claim is made about whether the reader policies have drifted. This change does not touch the reader role, so those bindings are unaffected either way.

two_state_model.contained: narrow Allow present + Deny present -> effective explicit Deny
two_state_model.released: narrow Allow present + Deny removed -> effective Allow to exactly the governed reader role
two_state_model.rationale: the Allow is the permanent base capability; the Deny is the latch. Only one statement moves at execution time.
